inputs.original_text: This is a power grab dressed up as legal reform. They’re pushing changes to Cyprus’ surveillance law that would remove judicial oversight, with a House vote expected Thursday—and the fact it was discussed in a closed session tells you how much they want scrutiny kept out of sight. Lawyers are warning about it, but the people steering this clearly see accountability as an obstacle. The secrecy isn’t incidental; it’s part of the plan.
inputs.modified_text: They’re calling it legal reform, but the real aim is to make surveillance easier to control from the top by removing judicial oversight. A closed-door discussion and a House vote expected Thursday are not signs of an open process—they’re how you keep the public from seeing who benefits. The lawyers’ warnings are being brushed aside because accountability is exactly what this arrangement is designed to bypass. The secrecy is the tell.
